summary: Feed s051_single is degraded: 32.2% of TCP sessions (68/211) are one-way, violating NDR requirement for bidirectional traffic. All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, drops, overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / SPAN is forwarding only one direction of traffic to the NDR port. Likely only ingress or egress is tapped, or RX/TX from a TAP pair are not aggregated, or asymmetric routing sends return path via a different link that is not captured. 68 of 211 sessions show single direction, well above 10% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly, flow correlation and detection. With 32.2% one-way sessions the NDR cannot reconstruct sessions, will miss lateral movement, C2 and data exfiltration, and will generate incomplete flow records and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions (RX and TX / ingress and egress) from the TAP/SPAN pair and hash both sides of a flow to the same NDR tool port so the NDR sees complete bidirectional sessions for detection coverage.
